idiom_name: fragment functions appending to a growable output buffer (open_memstream)
implementation_notes: C has no template facility, so the pattern is built by hand: each fragment is a function that appends its markup to a growable output buffer (open_memstream(), or a hand-rolled char* + capacity buffer), and the page function calls the fragments in region order, passing the model explicitly - the call sites are the placeholders and the page function is the View Manager. Static regions can be emitted with fputs/fprintf format strings, but only keeping the markup inside fragment functions makes it reusable; where templates must be edited without recompiling, a Mustache-style engine ({{> partial}}) is the alternative that supplies resolution and partial lookup.
pitfalls: sprintf/fprintf into a fixed char buffer without snprintf() bounds is the classic page-composition overrun; render into a growable buffer (open_memstream) or respect snprintf's return value and the truncation semantics.
Layout markup as C string literals has no escaping: interpolating a user-supplied name without a dedicated escape helper is an XSS hole, and fragments must not close or free the shared FILE*/buffer.
Nothing links a fragment function name to its call site at compile time, and there is no template caching to add later - cost per region is whatever the function does per request.
